messages:
Priya (support): FYI, Acme engineering just opened a high-sev ticket — they see p99 latency jump ~3x since ~21:50 UTC and a handful of 504s. Their app saw timeouts. Our p95 panel looks flat. https://acme.ticket/12345
Devon (oncall): ack. Do we have a customer-impacting alert?
Carla (eng-sre): not from alerts — p99 alert didn't fire because it uses the rollup job by default. I can start looking at raw histograms.
Marcus (observability): I'm pulling both the dashboard queries now. Quick note: we rolled metrics-lib v2.1.0 to prod at 21:58 last night (deploy-bot shows deploy to core-metrics). Could be related.
deploy-bot: "deploy metrics-lib v2.1.0 -> service: core-metrics, at 2026-02-07T21:58:10Z, sha: b7f3a2c"
Alice (backend): any schema changes in that release?
Marcus (observability): v2.1.0 introduced histogram bucket normalization to match upstream prometheus conventions — it changes boundary handling for aggregated histograms. The release note said 'align bucket fold behavior with histogram_v2'.
Priya (support): Acme says p99 for their /generate endpoint spiked from ~180ms to ~650ms, and errors started at 22:05 UTC. They also provided traces showing long backend queue waits.
Devon (oncall): Carla, can you compare raw histogram quantiles vs. our rollup quantiles for the same time window? Maybe rollup calc dropped some outliers.
Carla (eng-sre): running now. Queries I ran: PromQL raw: quantile_over_time(0.99, histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))) — then compared to our precomputed p99 timeseries.
Carla (eng-sre): Initial pass: raw histogram-based quantile (from scrape) shows a large spike at 22:02–22:08. Our rollup-derived p99 series is muted and shows a smaller bump at 22:10. The timing mismatch looks like the rollup windowing + histogram normalization caused sample loss.
Marcus (observability): I inspected the bucket boundaries before/after 21:58. Before: boundaries were powers-of-two-ish for latency buckets. After: bucket normalization collapsed some high-latency bins so top-end samples folded into a single top bucket. That makes histogram_quantile produce higher p99 on raw but our rollup aggregator (which re-buckets summaries) produced different smoothing.
Alice (backend): So which is closer to reality for customer requests? Raw histograms from app side or aggregated rollup?
Devon (oncall): We should treat raw per-instance histograms as ground truth for latency distribution. Rollups are approximations meant for long-term dashboards.
Priya (support): Acme wants action — they saw timeouts. Do we have a mitigation?
Carla (eng-sre): Short-term: 1) revert metrics-lib normalization to v2.0.9 on core-metrics to restore previous bucketing (rollback deploy). 2) Update alerting to also track raw-instance p99 for the affected endpoints to avoid missing regressions.
Marcus (observability): Agreed. Also we need to patch the rollup aggregator to preserve top buckets by using explicit 'infinity' bucket folding instead of re-normalizing. I'll open a ticket.
Devon (oncall): Can we do a targeted rollback to v2.0.9 without touching other services? If deploy-bot shows just core-metrics change, that should be safe.
Alice (backend): I can cut the rollback release. Preparing commands now.
Alice (backend): rollback command: 
```
kubectl -n observability set image deployment/core-metrics core-metrics=image-registry/redwood/core-metrics:v2.0.9
kubectl rollout status deployment/core-metrics
```
Carla (eng-sre): I'll watch the dashboards and the customer ticket. Also going to run a quick synthetic load against /generate to reproduce the latency pattern locally with both histogram configs.
Marcus (observability): I'm also exporting a side-by-side CSV of bucket counts pre/post for 21:30–22:30 to attach to the postmortem.
deploy-bot: "rollback core-metrics -> v2.0.9 initiated by Alice at 2026-02-07T22:35:12Z"
Priya (support): Acme reports initial improvement at 22:45 — p99 dropped back down to ~200ms and errors stopped. They're monitoring.
Devon (oncall): Good. Next: create a follow-up to ensure alerting covers both rollup and raw histograms for critical endpoints and add a dashboard note when deploying metrics-lib.
Carla (eng-sre): Action items assigned: 
- Marcus: bug ticket for aggregator folding behavior + tests (obs-3421).
- Alice: post rollback verification and co-ordinate a canary deploy with expanded histogram retention (backend-789).
- Devon: update runbook for latency alerting to include raw-histogram checks.
- Priya: keep Acme updated and draft incident summary for CS.
Devon (oncall): For the runbook change, add an example PromQL snippet to compute instance-level p99: 
```
quantile(0.99, sum by (instance)(rate(request_latency_bucket{endpoint="/generate"}[5m])))
```
Carla (eng-sre): Note for postmortem: root cause likely the metrics-lib normalization interacting with our rollup aggregator's re-bucketing implementation, resulting in delayed or smoothed p99 in the rollup timeseries while raw histograms preserved the spike.
Marcus (observability): I'll include diffs for histogram boundaries + a test harness to validate quantile parity after any future metrics-lib upgrade.
Priya (support): Customer satisfied with rollback but wants a proactive note before any metrics-related deploys. Can we add a small policy?
Alice (backend): Yes — add a checklist item to the release template: "Does this change histogram boundaries or bucket folding?" If yes, require a 1-hour canary and notify support.
Devon (oncall): Thanks all. I'll file the incident and set severity to P2 since it caused customer-visible errors but was resolved quickly.
Priya (support): Thanks — I'll close the ticket once Acme confirms 24h stability. :thumbsup:
